what_worked: Power-law thesis and missingness-as-signal framing show genuine analytical thinking worth developing further.
fix_next: Verify every headline number against the actual dataset; $334M total revenue is ~21× the real $15.6M, poisoning every downstream claim.
verdict: Strong narrative arc built on fabricated numbers; accuracy failures undermine the whole deck.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2/3: Total revenue stated $334M, actual $15.6M (~21× inflated). Slide 2/3: Top-10 share stated 61%, actual ~49.6%. Slide 3: Pareto percentile breakdown (61/19/10/7/3) unverifiable and likely fabricated from wrong base. Slide 5: US 70% revenue share plausible direction but unverifiable against wrong total; 258 startups matches but 241 missing country not disclosed. Slide 6: E-Commerce stated $54.8M from 19 startups; actual E-comm total ~$1.1M; AI actually has highest total revenue ($2.36M), not E-Commerce — category ranking inverted. Slide 7: Stripe revenue share stated 96%, actual ~87% ($13.5M/$15.6M). Slide 9: B2B median 4× B2C; reference shows median multiples ~2.35×. Slide 8: 20% zero revenue stated; reference shows 216 zero-revenue rows = 21.6%, close but '10% never earned a dollar' is unverifiable additional claim.

evidence.insight: Power-law concentration thesis is genuinely interesting and directionally correct; AI-vs-commerce tension is a good question but answer is factually inverted; stealth-company observation on slide 4 is original.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: hook → shape → gaps → winners → takeaways. Slide 10 synthesizes five points coherently. Sequence is purposeful. But the narrative rests on fabricated numbers, so the story told is fiction.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets date and sample size. Slide 4 addresses missingness thoughtfully and suggests future data needs. However, no disclosure of 241 missing country values on slide 5, 274 missing category on slide 6, or 288 missing audience_type on slide 9. Target audience never stated.
evidence.accuracy: Foundational total revenue is wrong by 21×, cascading into every percentage and dollar figure. Category ranking is inverted. Stripe share overstated. B2B multiple inflated. At least 8 material factual errors across the deck.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark Gamma template. Only two real charts (slides 3, 6); slide 6 chart collapses all categories into one bar, hiding the actual distribution. Donut charts on slide 7 are adequate. Three slides carry large decorative AI illustrations with no analytical purpose. Heavy text density throughout.
evidence.ai_slop: Decorative AI illustrations (anime figure slide 2, Japanese-themed map slide 5, cityscape slide 1) are thematically disconnected from the data. Consulting-style framing ('cold open,' 'uncomfortable truths') is mildly inflated but not egregious.

change_reason: Lowered accuracy from 2.5 to 2.0 given 8 material errors including a 21× revenue fabrication that poisons every claim; lowered visual from 4.5 to 4.0 for decorative-only AI art and only two real charts across 10 slides; lowered framing from 5.5 to 5.0 for missing denominator disclosures on key slides; removed bonus point — stealth observation is interesting but not rare enough to warrant bonus given pervasive inaccuracy.
